result.summary: The street features continuous sidewalks on both sides with street lighting and mature trees, providing a basic level of pedestrian infrastructure. However, the environment lacks marked crossings at the visible intersection and traffic calming measures, and parked vehicles may obstruct sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

hazards.name: Unmarked Intersection
hazards.description: The intersection ahead lacks marked crosswalks, which may lead to unpredictable pedestrian crossing behavior and reduced driver awareness.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles and large tree trunks near the curb can obstruct sightlines between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side foreground and left side curb line

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks at the intersection to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions (bulb-outs) at the intersection to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility by moving pedestrians past the line of parked cars.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Introduce speed humps or cushions to manage vehicle speeds on this residential/mixed-use street.

result.summary: The image shows a mid-block pedestrian environment with a continuous paved sidewalk separated from the roadway by a narrow grass buffer and parallel-parked vehicles. The street frontage is dominated by a low wall and chain-link fence bordering a large surface parking lot, which limits natural surveillance and street-level activity.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb line obstruct the view between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers on the roadway, increasing risk during potential crossings.

hazards.name: Lack of Natural Surveillance
hazards.description: The blank frontage created by the parking lot wall and fence reduces 'eyes on the street', which can impact pedestrian security.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Planting street trees within the grass buffer would provide shade, improve the aesthetic quality of the walk, and help slow traffic by visually narrowing the street.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Installing lighting specifically oriented toward the sidewalk would improve visibility and safety for pedestrians at night.

result.summary: The street features continuous sidewalks on both sides with street trees and lighting, providing basic pedestrian infrastructure. However, the lack of lane markings and designated crossing points on a relatively wide roadway may encourage higher vehicle speeds and create uncertainty for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of Lane Markings
hazards.description: The absence of painted lane lines can lead to unpredictable vehicle positioning and may encourage higher speeds on the wide asphalt surface.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway extending into the distance

hazards.name: Absence of Pedestrian Crossings
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks visible in this stretch, requiring pedestrians to cross without designated priority or visibility aids.

interventions.title: Roadway Striping
interventions.description: Apply lane markings to clearly define travel lanes and parking zones, which helps organize traffic and can naturally reduce vehicle speeds.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, paved sidewalk adjacent to an institutional building, likely a school, separated by a metal fence. While the walkway is clear and continuous, there is no physical buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway edge.

hazards.name: Lack of sidewalk buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or buffer zone between the pedestrian walkway and the adjacent roadway edge at the bottom of the frame.
hazards.location_in_image: Bottom edge of the sidewalk along the curb line.
